review.summary: I reviewed only the supplied diff and did not run any tests. Based on the code shown, the earlier MAJOR finding looks fixed: unavailable /lp GET and HEAD requests are now checked in the proxy before streaming starts. They return a fixed anonymous 404 page, or 503 if the check itself fails. The merchant warning and missing-item links run only after the selected project and page are authorized, and the anonymous error page does not reveal why a page is unavailable. The earlier MINOR and NIT items appear handled: diagnosis errors no longer block the editor, unpublish refreshes the status, the public page id is compared, the payment check is not relaxed, and the status box has an aria label and uses slate/emerald/amber colors. I found no BLOCKER or MAJOR issues. What remains: (1) the merchant diagnosis does not run the same step and A/B checks as the proxy; (2) redirect decisions still go to the streaming route, so the HTTP status may be 200 instead of 30x; (3) the proxy may refuse system step paths; (4) only the route matcher keeps non-/lp paths out of the 404 check; (5) autosave triggers extra reads; plus small message-text issues. Code I could not see is described as unknown in the findings. No findings here certify that tests or a release pass.

findings.area: getLandingPagePublicationStatus, published branch (step-funnel checks after loadPublicLandingPage)
findings.issue: The merchant diagnosis does not run the same step and runtime checks as the proxy, so the merchant UI can say 'available' while anonymous visitors get a 404 (or the reverse).
findings.evidence: The proxy (publicLandingPageStatus) finds the first non-system step, checks getPublicFunnelPage(), calls resolvePublicFunnelRuntime() and checks the rendered step's page. The diagnosis instead checks steps.pages[step.id] for every non-system step plus funnelOperationsReferencesValid(), and never calls resolvePublicFunnelRuntime or getPublicFunnelPage. A runtime decision of 'unavailable', or a rendered A/B variant that getPublicFunnelPage rejects, gives 404 in the proxy but 'available: true' in the diagnosis.
findings.impact: A merchant can be told the public URL works when anonymous visitors get a 404, which defeats the 'warning when not public' requirement. The stated runtime-parity claim does not cover the diagnosis path.
findings.recommended_fix: Build the published-branch decision from publicLandingPageStatus(`/lp/${encodeURIComponent(slug)}`, <fixed diagnostic visitor id>), or from a shared predicate, and keep the merchant-only reason text in a separate step. Alternatively, use getPublicFunnelPage and resolvePublicFunnelRuntime in the diagnosis too.
findings.required_test: Fixture: project and funnel published, but the runtime returns 'unavailable' or the rendered variant step fails getPublicFunnelPage. Assert that the diagnosis returns available=false and the proxy returns 404 for the same slug.

findings.issue: Redirect (and deadline) decisions are passed to the streaming public route with status 200. Any redirect() the route makes after the root loading boundary starts streaming becomes a 200 response with a client-side redirect, not a real 30x.
findings.evidence: The comment says '截止與合法轉址仍交公開 route 呈現' (deadline and valid redirects are still rendered by the public route). This is the same mechanism that caused the earlier streamed-404-as-200 MAJOR. The proxy only produces 404 or 503 and never builds a redirect response.
findings.impact: For redirect steps, HEAD and non-JS clients or crawlers get 200 instead of 307/308. The proxy also doesn't validate the redirect target, so a broken redirect still produces a 200 followed by a not-found page. This is outside the required 404 scope, so it is not blocking.
findings.recommended_fix: For decisions that redirect, validate the target step and return NextResponse.redirect(...) from the proxy using the same URL the route would build. Otherwise, explicitly accept and document 200 for redirects.
findings.required_test: Live GET and HEAD on a funnel step whose runtime decision is a redirect: assert a 30x status and Location header (or the documented expected status), and a 404 when the redirect target has no public page.

findings.issue: The proxy returns 404 for any requested step path that belongs to a system step. If the existing /lp/[slug]/[step] route serves system steps (for example thank-you or confirmation steps reached after a form or checkout), this change newly returns 404 for them.
findings.evidence: The rendered-step check later does not filter on isSystem, so the two checks treat system steps differently. Test evidence lists only draft, disabled-form, invalid-ops (404) and published-form (200) cases; none request a system step path directly.
findings.impact: Post-conversion pages could start returning 404 to real visitors. This is unverifiable from the supplied scope because the route source is not shown.
findings.recommended_fix: Make the requested-step lookup match the existing public route's rule exactly, ideally by reusing the route's step-resolution helper instead of adding the !isSystem filter.
findings.required_test: GET and HEAD on /lp/<slug>/<system-step-path> for a published funnel: assert the same status before and after the proxy change.

findings.issue: The proxy calls publicLandingPageStatus for every GET or HEAD that reaches it, and that function returns 404 for any path not under /lp. Only the matcher config (not shown in the diff) keeps other paths out of this check.
findings.evidence: publicLandingPageStatus: `if (segments[0] !== "lp" ...) return 404;`. The proxy maps 404 straight to publicUnavailable(). The comment '限 /lp…其他入口不載入 DB 模組' (limited to /lp; other entry points don't load the DB module) suggests other paths may reach the proxy, yet the code has no pathname check of its own.
findings.impact: If the matcher is ever widened (or already covers non-/lp marker routes), every GET or HEAD to those paths gets a hard 404 and a database read.
findings.recommended_fix: Add an explicit check `if (!request.nextUrl.pathname.startsWith("/lp/")) skip preflight` before the dynamic import.
findings.required_test: Unit test the proxy with GET on a non-/lp path covered by the matcher. Assert no 404 and that the status module is not imported.

findings.issue: The diagnosis loads display data it doesn't need, and it runs after every action, including each step-metadata autosave.
findings.evidence: includePresentation defaults to true, so the commerce lookup and publicConsultationEvents run. successWithPublication wraps saveLandingPageStepMetadata (autosave), so each autosave also runs 5 gate queries or the full public load.
findings.impact: Extra database load and slower autosave responses in the editor, with no change to the diagnosis result.
findings.recommended_fix: Pass includePresentation=false in the diagnosis. Consider skipping or debouncing the publication refresh for autosave.
findings.required_test: Spy test: the diagnosis call does not run commerce or consultation event queries, and the result matches the current one.

findings.issue: The unpublished-project message has no closing '。', and every action message, autosave included, now repeats the status already shown in the role=status section.
findings.evidence: message: "專案尚未發布，公開網址目前無法開啟" (no '。'), while the other messages end with '。'. The action builds `${message}${publication.message}`, and the workspace also shows publication.message in a role="status" section.
findings.impact: Run-on text such as '草稿已儲存。專案尚未發布，公開網址目前無法開啟', and screen readers may announce the same status twice.
findings.recommended_fix: Add '。' to the message, and either drop the appended publication text from the action message or remove role=status from one of the two places.
findings.required_test: Component test: after saving, the publication message appears once in the accessible live region.

findings.issue: The catch-all turns any other error into the fallback status, including Next.js redirect or notFound control-flow errors that editorProject() might throw.
findings.evidence: Only LandingPageNotFoundError and LandingPageScopeError are handled specially; every other error returns the fallback object.
findings.impact: Low. Later editor loads probably repeat the auth or scope redirect, but redirect handling now depends on call order.
findings.recommended_fix: Rethrow Next.js navigation errors (e.g. via unstable_rethrow) before returning the fallback.
findings.required_test: With a session that triggers editorProject redirect, assert the page still redirects.
